new: This is not primarily a willingness problem. Tanzanians report strong tax morale: 65.7% say good citizens should always pay the taxes they owe, and 81.2% trust the tax office at least somewhat [COMPUTED] (Afrobarometer, 2021). Yet only 3.83% of adults hold a Taxpayer Identification Number [COMPUTED]. Two barriers stand between willingness and registration. The first is friction: 64.9% find it difficult even to find out which taxes they are supposed to pay [COMPUTED]. The second is voice: only 23.1% say their local councillors listen to people like them, 42.6 percentage points below the share who see paying tax as a duty [COMPUTED]. The challenge is therefore not persuading citizens that tax matters. It is building a continuous relationship that removes friction and makes reciprocity visible, carrying existing willingness into the formal tax system and keeping it there.
